scientific_disciplines_widely_cited_scientists staged — ready for audit

Adapted seed #19 with all cycles 1+2+3 lessons applied upfront.

Files written:

- datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/scientific_disciplines_widely_cited_scientists.draft.json

Schema: Discipline(key) | List Position(numeric, non-key) | Scientist(key) | Nationality(text) | Era(text) | Contribution(text). Composite PK = (Discipline, Scientist).

Universe + value sources (26 Wikipedia URLs):
- 1 universe anchor: "Branches of science" → 5 disciplines (Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics, Astronomy)
- 25 per-scientist Wikipedia articles (5 per discipline × 5 disciplines), each cited from cycle 0 with verbatim quotes in the Roles: block

Per-discipline picks (chronological by birth year within each):
- Physics: Newton, Faraday, Maxwell, Einstein, Bohr
- Chemistry: Lavoisier, Dalton, Mendeleev, Curie, Pauling
- Biology: Linnaeus, Darwin, Pasteur, Mendel, Watson
- Mathematics: Euclid (fl. 300 BC), Euler, Gauss, Riemann, Hilbert
- Astronomy: Copernicus, Kepler, Galileo, Herschel, Hubble

Cycles 1+2+3 lessons applied upfront (avoiding the citation-expansion grind seen in twentieth_century_decade_inventions):
- Selection-not-ranked framing in title from cycle 0
- PK (Discipline, Scientist) with List Position non-key from cycle 0
- Per-row Wikipedia article cited from cycle 0
- No duplicate scientists across disciplines (Newton only in Physics; Galileo only in Astronomy; Curie only in Chemistry)

Diversity: 12 distinct nationality values (English, Scottish, Italian, French, Russian, Polish, Polish-French, German, German-born, German-British, Danish, Swedish, Austrian, American, Swiss, Ancient Greek). Era spans fl. 300 BC (Euclid) → 1928-2025 (Watson, very recent death — flagged as temporal-edge risk).

Creator preflight: 25/25 OK including 3 cycle-2-lessons-upfront checks (PK, List Position type, title framing) and the universal-from-cycle-0 PK uniqueness + no-duplicate-scientists checks.

Snapshot updated: instance_selection_priorities.md shows scaled_enumeration staged 3→4, Science family 2→3, seed #19 touched, queue head shifted to #23 Nobel categories × last 5 laureates (Science/Academia).

Three open questions for the auditor: (1) curator-chosen 5-discipline universe (vs the wider Branches of science classification); (2) hybrid nationalities (Einstein, Curie, Herschel, Copernicus) followed each article's primary phrasing; (3) Watson's 2025 death year is post-cutoff for some LLMs — temporal-edge risk documented.

Full pre-registration sweep: NOT READY — 2 BLOCKING findings.

Counts by severity: BLOCKING=2 / NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE=0 / SUGGESTION=1
Counts by issue type: factual=0 / structural=0 / scope-related=3

What passes:
- Local table mechanics: 25 rows x 6 columns; exactly 5 rows per discipline; List Position values are 1-5 inside each discipline; duplicate count for primary_key=(Discipline, Scientist) is 0; no scientist appears in more than one discipline partition.
- Schema and metadata mechanics: CSV header matches draft.columns; column_types cover exactly the six columns; source_count=26 equals len(source_urls); query_category=scaled_enumeration and operation_type=union+filter are plausible for a partitioned selected-list table; gt_construction=manual_wikipedia; domain=Science/History of Science fits the domain taxonomy.
- Sampled row-value support is strong: Watson's article supports American / 1928-2025 / DNA double helix (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Watson, lead, lines 310-311); Marie Curie's article supports Polish-French, 1867-1934, and polonium/radium/radioactivity (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marie_Curie, infobox/lead, lines 316-348 and 404-405); Euclid/Euler/Galileo/Hubble samples likewise support the staged field/era/contribution values from their individual pages. The cycle-0 per-row citation choice avoided the value-source gaps seen in the prior invention instance.

Findings:

1. (scope-related, BLOCKING) The cited source set does not support the row-universe claim "five widely-cited scientists" per discipline.

The staged title asks the model to list "five widely-cited scientists" for each named discipline, and curation.json marks the instance as source_defined. But the cited source set has only one discipline-universe page plus 25 individual biography pages. The Branches of science page supports that the named disciplines are scientific disciplines: it divides science into formal/natural/social groups, names mathematics under formal sciences, and names physics/chemistry/astronomy and biology under natural sciences (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branches_of_science, lead/formal/natural-science sections, lines 209-214, 223-225, and 300-301). It does not define the five scientists selected within any discipline. The individual scientist pages support Nationality/Era/Contribution values, but they do not establish that these are the five "widely-cited" scientists for the discipline, nor do they provide a citation-count or ranked/selected-list criterion.

The curation record itself describes the selections as curator-chosen. That is a useful construction note, but it is not source-defined ground truth for the row universe. Under the audit policy, this materially affects the row universe and claim type: many other equally plausible candidates could replace current rows without contradicting the cited sources.

Minimal repair: either (a) add authoritative source(s) that actually define the five-per-discipline scientist set or a measurable citation/influence rule and rebuild rows to match that rule; or (b) change the instance to an honestly anchored source-defined query whose row set is directly recoverable from a cited list/table. If keeping curator-chosen rows, change claim_type away from source_defined and mark this as candidate_rebuild / not registration-ready.

2. (scope-related, BLOCKING) The Watson row uses a 2025 death year that is source-correct but violates the benchmark's LLM-knowable fit for pre-2025 parametric models.

CSV row: Biology / James Watson / Era=1928-2025. The staged ground-truth source supports the value: James Watson's article gives April 6, 1928 to November 6, 2025 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Watson, lead, line 310). The problem is benchmark scope, not factual accuracy. The protocol requires instances to be plausibly answerable from parametric knowledge with a pre-2025 cutoff, and the curation note itself says older models may know Watson as living. Because Era is an evaluated column, a pre-2025 model can be penalized for not knowing a post-cutoff death event in an otherwise low-temporal-sensitivity historical table.

Minimal repair: replace Watson with a similarly foundational pre-cutoff biology figure, or normalize the Era column to a cutoff-stable form such as "20th-21st century" / "1928-" and document the matching policy. If retaining exact birth-death ranges, set temporal_sensitivity higher and reconsider whether the instance is fair for the intended benchmark population.

3. (scope-related, SUGGESTION) Wiki-family discovery found broader list pages, but they do not solve the top-five selection problem by themselves.

Validation/challenge sources found during the bounded Wiki-family pass include List of physicists and List of astronomers. These pages explicitly define broad notable-person universes, not top-five or citation-ranked lists: List of physicists says it is a dynamic list and then lists physicists notable for achievements (validation source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_physicists, lead, lines 123-128), while List of astronomers lists astronomers and other notable people who contributed to astronomy (validation source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_astronomers, lead, lines 161-167). These pages could be cited as optional validation-role sources for discipline membership, but using them without a ranking/filtering convention would still leave the current five-person selections curator-chosen.

Cardinality and partition sanity:
- The asserted shape is internally consistent: 5 disciplines x 5 scientists = 25 rows.
- The total and per-partition row counts are correct, but correct cardinality does not cure the source-defined row-universe issue. The table can have exactly 25 rows while still omitting equally plausible in-scope candidates because no cited source defines which five belong.

Final judgment: Not ready. The CSV is mechanically clean and the per-row biography values are well cited, but the row-universe / selection claim and Watson temporal-edge issue block registration.

Minimal fixes needed:
1. Add or switch to source(s) that define the five scientists per discipline, or rebuild the instance around a truly source-defined list/table.
2. Change claim_type if the row set remains curator-chosen; source_defined is too strong for the current source plan.
3. Repair the Watson Era issue by replacing the row or using a cutoff-stable era representation.
4. After repair, update source_coverage_notes, decision_log, temporal_note, and audit_response.cycle_1, then rerun preflight.

List of chemists states its inclusion criterion is importance to chemistry and includes Pauling (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_chemists, lead and Pauling entry, lines 118 and 765-770). List of biologists includes Linnaeus, Pasteur, and Mendel (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_biologists, entries at lines 1072, 1269-1270, and 1135). List of astronomers defines a broad notable-astronomy list (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_astronomers, lines 163-168). Lists of mathematicians is a list-of-lists index for notable mathematicians (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lists_of_mathematicians, lines 141-180).

Findings:

1. (scope-related, BLOCKING) The source plan still does not support the title's “five widely-cited scientists” selection rule.

The cycle-1 repair upgrades the source plan from individual biographies only to discipline-membership lists, which is real progress. But the title still asks for “five widely-cited scientists” per discipline, while the cited list pages define broad notable membership, not citation frequency or a five-person selection. List of physicists explicitly says it is dynamic and may be incomplete, then lists physicists notable for achievements; it is not a citation-ranked or top-K list (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_physicists, lines 125-128). List of astronomers likewise says it lists notable contributors to astronomy and includes prize/technique/observatory examples, not citation-ranked scientists (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_astronomers, lines 163-168). List of chemists says it includes people important to chemistry's development or practice, again not “widely cited” or top five (staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_chemists, line 118). The curation record still describes the five rows per discipline as “curator's display choice” from those broad lists (local locator: datasets/pkdb_bench/staging/scientific_disciplines_widely_cited_scientists.curation.json, source_coverage_notes / audit_response.cycle_1).

This materially affects the row universe because many other list members could satisfy “notable scientist in the discipline,” and the current source set does not distinguish why these five are the expected answer to “widely-cited.” Prior selected-list precedents are closer when the source page itself emphasizes the selected entries; here the new list pages are large alphabetical/notability universes, so the “widely-cited” wording remains unsupported.

Minimal repair: either (a) change the title and metadata to an honest selected-list query, e.g. “For each of five major scientific disciplines, list five selected foundational scientists...” and explicitly define the row set as curator-selected from source-defined notable membership; or (b) add/rebuild from sources with an actual citation/influence/top-scientist rule per discipline. If keeping “widely-cited,” the source plan needs citation/ranking evidence.

2. (scope-related, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) Narrative overstates the new list pages as confirming all membership rows in a few places.

The added pages generally support broad discipline membership, but some curation prose still says or implies direct confirmation where the cited page is only an index or where the role note relies on “implicit” / “universally listed” language. The clearest case is Mathematics: Lists of mathematicians is a list-of-lists index and a find on the page does not show Euclid, Euler, Riemann, Gauss, or Hilbert directly; the actual direct evidence that each row is a mathematician is in the per-scientist pages. Local locator: curation.json::source_coverage_notes source_urls[30]; staged ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lists_of_mathematicians, lines 141-180. This does not add a second blocker because the per-scientist pages support the values and discipline identity, but the role language should be tightened.

Minimal cleanup: rewrite the list-source roles as broad membership/index anchors, and say direct row-value support comes from the per-scientist articles unless the list page visibly names that scientist.

Final judgment: Not ready. The Watson cutoff issue is fixed and the table is mechanically clean, but registration should wait until the title/source-scope mismatch around “widely-cited” is resolved.

Minimal fixes needed:
